<!-- Theme bootstrap: apply saved theme BEFORE styles render to avoid flash -->
<script>
(function(){
  // v794.3 — this used to default to 'light' while getTheme() defaulted to
  // 'dark'. With nothing saved, boot marked the page light, then applyTheme
  // ran and removed the body class but LEFT data-theme="light" on <html>, so
  // body-class rules went dark while html[data-theme] rules stayed light —
  // a half-dark screen. Both defaults must agree, and both flags must always
  // be written together. Keep this in sync with getTheme().
  try {
    var saved = localStorage.getItem('fc_theme') || 'dark';
    var t = saved === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
    if (saved === 'flame') localStorage.setItem('fc_theme', 'dark');
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', t);
    if (t === 'light') {
      // Body doesn't exist yet — mirror the selected appearance once it does.
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function(){
        document.body.classList.add('theme-light');
      });
    }
  } catch (e) {}
})();
</script>
<script>
/* v1100 — shared motion preference. Challenge-card video snippets intentionally
   remain enabled; this helper is for scrolling and decorative motion only. */
function fcPrefersReducedMotionV1100() {
  return !!(window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches);
}
function fcMotionBehaviorV1100() {
  return fcPrefersReducedMotionV1100() ? 'auto' : 'smooth';
}
</script>

     installed PWA has no address bar, leaving NO way to refresh short of
     force-quitting. Keep -x contained so horizontal card scrolls can't
     jitter the page; allow -y so the native gesture works. */

/* ============ NAV ============ */
.nav {
  /* v804 — was position:sticky. Sticky only holds inside its PARENT, and the
     parent is #appView, an ordinary div that scrolls with the document — so the
     nav rode off the top with it and whatever came next (the Challenges search
     field) landed under the status bar. Three rounds of padding tweaks on the
     content below were aimed at the wrong element. fixed + a matching top
     offset on #appView is the actual fix. */
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 100;
  /* v761 — viewport-fit=cover means the page runs under the status bar /
     Dynamic Island. In Safari the browser chrome absorbed that, so nothing
     needed this; installed as a PWA the app owns the full screen and the
     nav buttons ended up UNDER the island — drawn, but not tappable (taps
     go to the system). The inset is 0 in Safari, so this is a no-op there. */
  padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top);
  backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(140%);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(140%);
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.75);
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
}
body.theme-light .nav { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88); border-bottom-color: var(--border); }
/* The nav is fixed, so #appView needs its height reserved. Padding (not margin)
   so backgrounds still run to the top edge. */
/* v805 — .nav-inner is 58px and .nav has a 1px bottom border: 59px total.
   Reserved exactly that, plus scroll-padding so anchor jumps and focus()
   calls never land content under the fixed header either. */
:root { --nav-h: calc(59px + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)); }
#appView { padding-top: var(--nav-h); }
html { scroll-padding-top: var(--nav-h); }

/* Feed item: challenge tile (mini card style) */
/* ---------- v802 · challenge card (step 4) ---------- */
/* .feed-challenge-card is a flex container (column). Its children do NOT
   automatically take the full width, so blocks with no intrinsic content —
   the empty-state frame and the winner image — collapsed to 0px. Every direct
   block of the card stretches explicitly. */
.chc-top,.chc-title,.chc-strip,.chc-empty,.chc-win,.chc-fin,.chc-meta,.chc-cta{
  width:100%;align-self:stretch;box-sizing:border-box;flex:0 0 auto}
/* v804 — a subtle boundary so each card reads as one object in the feed, and
   media tiles ~18% shorter (square → 5:4) so a screen fits more cards without
   losing what the entries are. */
.fcc-challenge-wrap{border:1px solid var(--border);box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.03) inset,0 6px 18px -12px rgba(0,0,0,.8)}
.chc-top{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:9px}

.fcc-entries-scroll {
  /* v708 — snap lives HERE now, not under #feedContainer. v673 added snap to fix
     the feed and scoped it to #feedContainer, leaving the Challenges page — the
     same component — with none, so it coasted to a stop mid-card. v673's own
     comment said "every other horizontal pager in the app snaps"; it just never
     fixed its twin. One rule, both surfaces. */
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
  /* v722 — 16px, matching the `padding:16px` BOTH challenge-card renderers write
     inline (feed 19169, challenges page 16084). The entry row is the only thing
     in the card that isn't the card's own text, and it has to start on the same
     line as the title or the card reads as off-centre. */
  scroll-padding-left: 16px;
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: nowrap; /* critical — prevent wrapping to grid */
  gap: 8px;
  overflow-x: auto !important;
  overflow-y: hidden;
  -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
  /* v710 — was `pan-x`, which does NOT mean "prefer horizontal": it means this
     element accepts ONLY horizontal panning, so a vertical drag starting on a
     card was discarded instead of scrolling the page. The scroller is 418px tall
     (4/5 media), so that dead zone covers most of a card — you had to find the
     gap between cards to scroll the feed.
     `pan-x pan-y` keeps horizontal scrolling here AND lets vertical reach the
     page; iOS direction-locks on the initial gesture, so a horizontal swipe
     still won't jitter the page vertically. overscroll-behavior-x: contain
     already stops horizontal overscroll leaking to the page. */
  touch-action: pan-x pan-y;
  overscroll-behavior-x: contain;
  will-change: scroll-position;
  padding: 0 16px 8px; /* v722 — matches the card's 16px content padding */
  scrollbar-width: none;
  margin-bottom: 8px;
  width: 100%;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
.fcc-entries-scroll::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }

/* v747 — dot pager under the entry row. Active dot stretches to a pill (the
   iOS/Instagram convention) so position is readable at a glance. The ::after
   inset gives each 6px dot a ~24px tap target without changing the visual. */

.fcc-dot.active { width: 18px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--ember); }

.fcc-entry-card {
  scroll-snap-align: start; /* v708 — was #feedContainer-only; the card is the snap target everywhere */
  scroll-snap-stop: always;
  will-change: transform;
  /* v708 — ONE WIDTH FOR BOTH SURFACES. This said 72vw while the feed renderer
     wrote `flex:0 0 83vw!important` INLINE, so the same component measured 334px
     in the feed and 280px on the Challenges page. The inline rule is gone; this
     is the only place entry width is set now. That also removes the trap the
     v673 block warns about — an inline !important that silently beat every
     stylesheet edit (v673, v675 and v693 all lost to it).
     v700 REVERTED v693's narrowing (46vw / 185px) back to 72vw.
     v693 measured a Facebook ad carousel at ~193px and matched it. The
     measurement was right and the conclusion was wrong: an FB ad tile is built
     to be glanced past, while an ENTRY is the product — people are here to judge
     it and vote. At 185px a video entry is too small to evaluate, so every vote
     costs a tap-through and the in-feed row stops earning its space.
     It also made the row look broken: at 185px two entries fit on screen
     (2x185+8 = 378 of 402), so with 2 entries nothing overflowed and the
     horizontal scroll appeared to have been removed. At 72vw+ a second entry
     always overflows, so the row always reads as scrollable.
     Arena items are media-forward. Don't re-narrow this to match a feed whose
     job is passive scrolling. */
  /* v747 — ONE ENTRY PER SCREEN. The 83vw peek above was a deliberate carousel
     affordance, but it read as a rendering glitch (a sliver of the next photo
     inside the current frame) rather than as "there's more". Replaced with the
     conventional pattern: full-width card + a dot pager underneath, which says
     the same thing explicitly. The v700 concern that drove 83vw — a row that
     doesn't LOOK scrollable — is answered by the dots, not by the sliver. */
  flex: 0 0 100%;
  min-width: 100%;
  max-width: none;
  background: var(--bg-2);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.fcc-entry-media {
  /* v709 — was `height: 120px`, hard-coded. v673 replaced it with a 4/5 aspect
     ratio but scoped that to #feedContainer, so the Challenges page kept the
     120px letterbox: the same entry rendered 334x418 in the feed and 334x120
     here. v673's own note called height:120px the bug it was fixing — it just
     fixed one of the two surfaces. Base rule now; both get it. */
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  aspect-ratio: 4 / 5;
  object-fit: cover; display: block;
  background: var(--bg-2);
}
